stories.title: Datacentres are deeply unpopular. Has Sweden made one we can all love?
stories.summary: A wooden data centre in Falun, Sweden, is being presented as a more community-minded model for an often unpopular industry. Operated by EcoDataCenter, the facility resembles a large Ikea building, runs entirely on renewable power and was designed with the local community in mind. Its features support a claim that it may be among the world's greenest data centres.

links.headline: Datacentres are deeply unpopular. Has Sweden made one we can all love?
links.excerpt: It is built of wood, resembles an Ikea and its power is totally renewable. Plus, it was built with the local community in mind. Is this facility in Falun the best datacentre in the world? ‘It was pretty cool, when they were building it. It looked like a very large Ikea,” says John Wernvik, of EcoDataCenter. He is giving me a tour of their facility in Falun, Sweden, which could lay claim to being the world’s greenest datacentre – although to many, that is a contradiction in terms.

stories.title: ‘To them, we’re just NPCs’: the artists and activists challenging Trump’s video game propaganda
stories.summary: Artists and activists are responding to the Trump White House's use of video-game imagery with satirical games of their own. The projects turn the gamification of politics back on the administration, including a game that asks the president to choose between ordering a Diet Coke and invading Iran. The work follows the White House's launch of Arcade, a collection of browser games based on familiar titles.

stories.title: NHS England deletes ‘misleading’ claim 137 trusts benefiting from Palantir AI tools
stories.summary: NHS England removed a website claim that 137 hospital trusts were benefiting from Palantir's AI health-data tools. The change followed a Guardian report that 29 of the listed trusts were not using all or most of the technology, making the original claim misleading.
